newsitem.title: LATVIA: REVIEW-ESTONIAN SHARES SURGE, LITHUANIA PICKS UP STEAM.
newsitem.headline: REVIEW-ESTONIAN SHARES SURGE, LITHUANIA PICKS UP STEAM.

text.p: Estonian shares surged to new highs over the past week, spurred by promising half-year results in the banking sector, while Lithuania's struggling market finally picked up some steam.
Latvia's bourse remained stuck in a rut ahead of six-month results which dealers hope will pull it out of the doldrums.
ESTONIA
Estonia's market roared upward, with shares hitting record highs for six straight sessions from July 3 to July 10.
Dealers cautioned that the red rags may fall and the market could be in for a slight short-term correction.
The Tasle index soared to 310.46 on Thursday from a close of 279.03 the previous Thursday as investors snapped up banking shares in response to a spate of solid results.
The region's leading bank, Hansapank , led the way, rising to 175.50 kroons at Thursday's close from 149.40 kroons week before.
Buying pressure from across the Gulf of Finland kept the momentum rolling as Finnish investors jumped on the Hansa bull run in Helsinki, where it is also quoted.
Forekspank , which raised its 1997 profit forecast by 24.6 million kroons to 96.4 million kroons, added almost eight kroons to 202.70 kroons over the week.
Dealers say the bank looks relatively cheap and has room to grow. Hoiupank added 20 kroons in the week to close at 174 kroons on Thursday.
Estonia, with its relatively advanced banking and financial sectors, remains by far the most liquid of the three Baltic bourses.
The presence of several asset management funds also gives the market a liquid edge over its neighbours.
LATVIA
Trade volumes remained extremely low on Latvia's bourse, though dealers took heart at the stabilisation of prices.
The recently introduced bourse index gained slightly over the week, to 385.78 from 384.92.
Traditional market leader Unibanka gave dealers some hope, as it inched up slightly. Brokers say it could lift the rest of the market if it mainatins a steady rise.

But a privatisation agency announcement that it planned to sell one million of the state's shares in the bank at a minumum price of 3.05 lats pulled its price down. The bank closed on Thursday at 3.36 lats and fell to 3.25 lats early Friday.

The local debt market and privatisation vouchers are still favoured over equities by local investors, who have taken a cautious approach in the wake of a long correction which set in after an early year surge.
LITHUANIA
Lithuania's illiquid bourse perked up after weeks of summer-induced inactivity although the market remained mixed.
The official index, which tracks the exchange's top five stocks, inched up steadily, rising to 922.6 on Thursday from 882.03 the previous week.
But the wider group A index remained stuck and eased a bit over the week to 1870.9 from 1874.16.
As in Estonia, banks lead the way.

Hermis Bank rose to 200 litas from 184 litas over the week as the market responded favourably to its six-month profit result of 14.3 million litas and its announcement that it was sticking to its 1997 profit forecast of 40.6 million litas.
Chief rival Vilniaus Bank closed at 240 litas on Thursday compared to 230 litas the previous week and dealers said the market would now focus on its upcoming results.
But some dealers said the bank's price looked right and did not expect it to rise much more.
